title: Salary Sacrifice Car Calculator Australia: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Use our salary sacrifice car calculator Australia to convert hourly rate to annual pay. Includes casual loading, super, and tax estimates for 2026-27 based on a 38-hour week.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week times 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How does a salary sacrifice car calculator Australia help with my hourly rate?
faqs.a: A salary sacrifice car calculator Australia lets you see how packaging a car affects your take-home pay. You start with your hourly rate, multiply by hours per week and 52 weeks to get annual gross. Then you can estimate the impact of salary sacrifice on your taxable income, remembering that super is paid on top of ordinary earnings and that salary sacrifice is not deducted in this basic estimate.

faqs.q: Does casual loading affect my annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Yes. Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. When you use the timesheet, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. The calculator then uses the loaded rate for the annual estimate. Remember that super is still paid on the ordinary earnings (base rate plus casual loading) at 12%.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a permanent employee, or $33.05 per hour including 25% casual loading. Award rates are industry-specific minimums set by the Fair Work Commission and are often higher. The salary sacrifice car calculator Australia uses the rate you enter, not a job median, so you should check your award or agreement for your correct base rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: The Simple Formula

To convert your hourly rate to an annual figure, use the standard formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For a full-time employee, the typical week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. So for a permanent employee on $30 per hour, the annual gross would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.

If you are a casual employee, you receive a 25% loading on top of your base rate. The timesheet on [the timesheet](/) lets you check a box to add that loading automatically. For the same $30 base rate, the casual rate becomes $37.50 per hour, and the annual gross becomes $37.50 × 38 × 52 = $74,100. Remember: never type a rate that already includes casual loading; let the calculator add it.

### Fortnightly Pay and Weekly Comparisons

Many employers pay fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the $30 permanent example: weekly pay is $30 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280. For casuals, weekly pay at $37.50 × 38 = $1,425, fortnightly $2,850. These figures help you compare with salary offers or budget using a **salary sacrifice car calculator Australia** if you are considering packaging a vehicle.

## Understanding the Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. That gives a weekly wage of $1,004.90 for 38 hours. Casual employees get $33.05 per hour including the 25% loading. However, many industries have award rates that are higher. The Fair Work Commission sets these awards, and you should check your specific award or agreement. This calculator does not use a job median; if you see an industry or state average from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, that is an average, not the median for your job. For example, ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, but that is an average across all full-time adults.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Casual loading compensates casual employees for not receiving paid leave. It is 25% of the base hourly rate. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (the super guarantee rate for 2026-27). Super is not deducted from your pay; your employer adds it separately. The maximum contribution base for super is $270,830 per year. If your annual ordinary earnings exceed that, super is only paid on the first $270,830.

For example, a casual employee on $30 base rate, annual gross $59,200 (using 38 hours). Super at 12% is $7,104, paid on top. The total cost to your employer is $66,304. If you use a **salary sacrifice car calculator Australia**, remember that salary sacrifice reduces your taxable income but does not affect the super guarantee calculation on your ordinary earnings.

## Tax and Medicare for 2026-27

The Australian Taxation Office resident tax rates for 2026-27 are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The Medicare levy surcharge applies if you do not have appropriate private hospital cover, but this calculator does not deduct it. The tax-free threshold is the full tax-free threshold is used. The Medicare reduction thresholds for singles are not confirmed for 2026-27, so we use the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds. This is an estimate, not a determination of your actual tax.

### Example Tax Estimate for a $74,100 Casual

Take a casual employee with annual gross $74,100 (from $30 base rate with 25% loading). Taxable income is $74,100. Tax on first $18,200 = $0; next $26,800 at 15% = $4,020; remaining $29,100 at 30% = $8,100; total tax $12,120. Medicare levy 2% = $1,482. Total tax plus Medicare = $13,602. Take-home pay = $60,498. Super on top at 12% = $8,892. This does not include salary sacrifice, HELP repayments, or the Medicare levy surcharge.

## Using the Timesheet and Other Resources

Start your conversion on [the timesheet](/) page. You can also refer to [pay guides](/blog) for award rates, [reference tables](/data) for tax brackets, and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more on salary sacrifice. If you are looking at a **salary sacrifice car calculator Australia**, the same hourly-to-annual formula applies, but you would then model the salary sacrifice reduction. Remember that salary sacrifice is not deducted in this basic estimate.

### Important Disclaimer

This annual pay estimate is an estimate only. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
